title: FlowTrigger
description: A wake-up intent contract. Declares when flow should resume or start work, but does NOT guarantee background execution. Plugins cannot invoke native /loop or scheduled tasks; FlowTrigger v3.0 is descriptive and command-driven (manual | hook | loop_prompt). Future v3.1+ adds github_actions / local_cron / local_daemon adapters.

suggested_interval.description: Human-readable interval suggestion (e.g., '20m', '1h'). Used by loop_prompt type to instruct the user-driven /loop.

user_starts_loop_manually.description: Set true for loop_prompt type — explicit acknowledgment that flow does NOT invoke /loop; the user does.

schedule.description: Cron expression — only valid for local_cron / github_actions types.

workflow.description: Workflow id (matches the FlowWorkflow metadata.id pattern). Pattern-constrained because trigger-policy interpolates this into plugins/flow/workflows/<workflow>.workflow.yaml during cross-reference — an unconstrained value is a path-traversal probe (cycle-14 SEC-6).

goal.description: Goal id (matches the FlowGoal metadata.id pattern).

command.description: Slash command to invoke when the trigger fires (e.g., /flow:run trigger pr-123-watch).

forbidden_actions.description: Hard requirement: must include 'merge' and 'release' (Tier 3 cannot be autonomous regardless of trigger settings). Enforced by schema: allOf contains assertions below.

stop_conditions.description: Boolean expressions evaluated each iteration. When all are true, the trigger should stop firing (terminal state).

recursion_policy.description: By default, triggered runs may NOT create or modify triggers — prevents trigger-creates-trigger loops.
